summary: Create Support macro/snippet library for standard customer comms (investigation/mitigation/closure) + restricted handling for sensitive accounts
description:
Background
As part of Escalation Playbook v2 rollout, we need a standardized macro/snippet library that Support/CS can use for consistent customer updates. Today macros are inconsistent across agents and occasionally include language that is not appropriate for restricted/sensitive accounts (Private/enterprise or security-adjacent incidents).

Goal
Create a centralized macro/snippet library for common customer comms templates (investigation started, mitigation applied, monitoring, RCA commitment, closure) with:
- Clear guidance on what is safe to share vs internal-only
- Restricted-handling rules for sensitive accounts/incidents
- Links back to Confluence templates + escalation playbook v2

Scope
- Jira (customer-support) macro/snippet set for:
  1) Acknowledgement / Investigation started
  2) Request for required fields (request_id, region, model, timestamp, SDK version)
  3) Mitigation applied / workaround provided
  4) Monitoring / next update timing
  5) RCA / follow-up commitment (without promising timelines we can’t meet)
  6) Resolution / closure
  7) Handoff to SRE / incident declared (customer-facing phrasing)
  8) Post-incident: status page + incident link language (when applicable)

Restricted handling requirements
- Add a “RESTRICTED” variant (or gating rules) for:
  - Private/VPC deployments
  - Security/SSO/audit-log related issues
  - Any account flagged as “restricted” by CS/Security
- Restricted versions must avoid:
  - internal system names (clusters, hostnames, shard IDs)
  - direct attribution of fault ("bug on our side") before confirmation
  - sharing other customers’ impact (“noisy neighbor”) unless explicitly approved
  - sharing incident IDs unless already publicly referenced / approved

Deliverables
- Macro/snippet library published in the Support macro tool (and mirrored in Confluence)
- Short agent-facing usage doc: when to use which macro + restricted handling decision tree
- Training note to include in Support rollout session

Acceptance criteria
- At least 8 macros available to Support in Jira customer-support project
- Each macro has:
  - title, intended use, and placeholders (e.g., {{customer_name}}, {{next_update_time}})
  - “safe-to-share” note + link to source Confluence template
- Restricted-handling guidance documented and reviewed by Security (Marcus Lin or Fiona McCarthy)
- Pilot with 3 Support agents and incorporate feedback

References
- Confluence: Escalation Playbook v2 → Customer comms templates
- Confluence: Status page + comms alignment (Support ↔ Incident updates)
- Related work: INT-1337 (new required fields/templates in Jira)

Notes
Do not include any customer-identifying examples in macro text. Keep language product-agnostic (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and avoid committing to ETAs unless we have a mitigation plan + SRE/Eng confirmation.
